# Pacing and structure

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

The film's shape: acts, holds, cadence, repeats that speed up, and one long hold where it counts. 17 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Each repeat runs faster

`ps-faster-each-repeat` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy medium · any

The first instance of a repeated action plays at full length, the second runs about 40% quicker, and later ones are implied or ratchet faster still.

- **Build:** Give the repeated component a duration parameter: dur_k = max(minDur, base * 0.6^k) for k = 0, 1, 2, and so on. It is the same curve compressed, so an E.out rise stays E.out. Show two full instances, then cut away or batch the rest. For lists, swaps and deletes, schedule start frames from shrinking gaps and pick the visible state with fd(frame). Across a film, the caption word stagger in src/fx/Words.tsx can fall the same way from the title to the last feature. Bind a repeat run with one low swell from the kit under the whole run (attack 6-9 f, release over about 84 f), with one tick per step growing by about 1 dB each time.
- **Timing:** Second instance at 0.6x length (for example a rise of 12 f becomes 7 f), starting about 46 f after the first. Ratchet gaps 26, 14, 12, 8, 8, 4, 4 f. Caption word stagger falling from 24 f on the title to 5 f on late captions.
- **Use when:** Repeated unlocks, card reveals, list items, word deletes, and captions that recur across a film.
- **Avoid when:** Items that each need a full read, and the first instance, which must teach the pattern at full length.

### Fixed-length ask, variable answer

`ps-fixed-ask-variable-answer` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

A demo repeats a fixed-length ask beat followed by a result whose length varies with its importance, so the rhythm teaches itself and the variations prevent fatigue.

- **Build:** Write the ask beat as one component with a fixed internal script, 6 beats long (180 f at 120 BPM). Typing takes 68 f however long the prompt is: visibleChars = fd(len * prog(f, 0, 68, E.linear)), with the first word pre-filled. Then an icon drop of 28 f, a chip morph of 16-20 f, cursor travel of 14 f on E.glide, a press of 32-40 f, and a plus-to-x rotation of 8-12 f as the cut cue. Results last 4-8 beats, and one hero result runs 2-3x the others. From the third cycle on, split the ask beat into a big-type or 3-4x close-up insert plus the card: the template stays and the framing changes.
- **Timing:** Ask beat 180-188 f (6 beats); results 138-234 f, the hero result about 490 f; 4-5 cycles; close-up insert from cycle 3.
- **Use when:** Prompt-to-result products, feature tours with one repeated action, and walkthroughs of 3-6 capabilities.
- **Avoid when:** Fewer than 3 instances (there is no pattern to learn), and stings.

### Image act, then type act

`ps-image-act-then-type-act` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy medium · feature, vertical

A short spot splits in half: the first half is pure imagery with no words at all, the second is pure type with no imagery.

- **Build:** Storyboard two contiguous ACTs at about 47/53%. Act 1 is three image shots of about 80 f each with no text layer at all, each ending on an accelerating exit (E.in). Act 2 is type only on a plain stage: the claim, then the headline, then the CTA and the lockup. Its first card continues act 1's screen direction across the seam. Keep text and imagery in separate Sequences so neither act can leak into the other, and run each type card on the breath envelope.
- **Timing:** Total 480-600 f. Act 1: 3 shots of 70-90 f. Act 2: claim 70-80 f, headline 60-70 f, CTA 60 f, then lockup 90-110 f.
- **Use when:** 6-12 s spots and social cut-downs with one claim and a strong visual metaphor, especially when watched on mute.
- **Avoid when:** Product walkthroughs that need captions on the UI, and films over 20 s.

### Light and dark as chapters

`ps-luma-act-map` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy any · launch, feature, walkthrough

Acts are planned by stage polarity, dark for the abstract or problem beats and light for the product, so chapter changes read without any title cards.

- **Build:** Add a LUMA map beside ACT in src/timeline.ts ('dark' or 'light' per act) and two stage token sets in src/brand/tokens.ts (dark at value 0.10-0.30, light at 0.85-0.95; the accent colour stays the same). Pick one plan. Alternation: about 50/50 dark and light, flipping at each ask/answer change. Arc: dark open, mixed middle, light product finish. Flips land on downbeats, 3-5 per film, and never use the same device twice in a row: an inverse hard cut, an inverse match cut on a shared icon, an iris from a glyph (20 f E.inOut), a bleach to white (26 f E.smooth), or a theme flip during a move (6 f). An optional second channel is a single-hue brand wash (one Background component with intensity 0-1) that shows only on brand beats: it rises from the bottom edge (translateY 40% to 0, 50 f E.out) and drains in 8 f E.in.
- **Timing:** 3-5 flips per film, each on b(n); iris 20 f E.inOut; bleach 26 f E.smooth; theme flip during a move 6 f; wash rise 50 f E.out, drain 8 f E.in.
- **Use when:** Films with distinct problem/solution or prompt/result halves, and 20-60 s pieces that need a rhythm at the scale of whole acts.
- **Avoid when:** Very short stings, and brands locked to a single stage colour.

### Long-tailed beat lengths

`ps-long-tail-beat-lengths` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy any · launch, walkthrough, feature

Beat lengths follow a long tail instead of an even grid: most beats sit near one median length, a few connective beats snap past at a third of it, and one or two hero beats run about three times as long, so the film never settles into a slideshow rhythm.

- **Build:** Before animating anything, write the cut list in src/timeline.ts as a BEATS array of cut-to-cut lengths in 8ths, and derive the ACT and CUE start frames from its running sum with b() so every boundary sits on the grid. Pick a median M of 60-72 f (2-2.4 beats at 120 BPM, inside the house shot median of 60-90 f) and fill the list from four bins. Core beats run 0.75-1.33x M (about 60%: features, claims, answers). Connective beats run 0.25-0.5x M and never under 24 f (about 20%: a punch-in insert, a whip, a one-word card, an isolate hold). Long beats run 1.5-2x M (10-15%: a walkthrough setup, a two-step interaction). One or two hero beats run 2.5-3x M, capped at 180 f, the house shot maximum (the hero result or the key feature), placed in the back half before the sign-off. Put one or two connective beats directly before each hero beat so the hero lands as a release, and never let three neighbouring beats sit within 10% of each other in length. Beats under 42 f carry no readable text (the copy rule is 36 f + 6 f per word). A hero beat is filled with continuous action, either a camera journey or a UI event at least every 40 f, never a long hold. Beside grid-check, add a node check asserting that max/M is 2.5-3.0, min/M is 0.16-0.5, no beat exceeds 180 f and the coefficient of variation is 0.4-0.8. An evenly spaced cut list scores about 0.1 and reads as a slideshow.
- **Timing:** M = 60-72 f. Connective beats 24-36 f (never under 24 f); core 0.75-1.33x M; long 1.5-2x M; hero 2.5-3x M, at most 180 f and at most 2 per film; coefficient of variation 0.4-0.8. Example 28.75 s cut at 120 BPM: 75, 60, 30, 75, 120, 45, 60, 75, 30, 75, 60, 45, 105, 60, 30, 180, 75, 45, 30, 180, 90 and 60 f, then a 120 f lockup (M 60, max/M 3.0, CV 0.56).
- **Use when:** Launch films and walkthroughs of 15 s or more with eight or more beats, any cut list that came out evenly spaced, and deciding where the hero feature gets its time.
- **Avoid when:** Polyrhythm loops and fixed-length ask cycles, where equal length is the point; stings under about 8 s, which have too few beats for a distribution; accelerando runs, which set their own length ratios.

### Loop seam hidden at a motion peak

`ps-loop-seam-on-motion-peak` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy medium · loop

A loop wraps around on the fastest frame of a whip or push, so the last frame flows into the first with no visible restart.

- **Build:** Make the clip length L a whole number of bars (for example 4 bars = 480 f at 120 BPM). Design frame 0 as the second half of a move, opening already travelling on E.out from full speed, and the last 12-24 f as the first half of the same move, an E.in ramp to the same speed and direction. Make every state a pure function of frame % L. Verify the seam by rendering frames L-2, L-1, 0 and 1: per-frame position deltas should match within 10%, and every discrete fd() state at L should equal frame 0. Wrap motion-blur sub-frame times modulo L so the seam frame smears like its neighbours, and loop the music bed on the same bar line.
- **Timing:** L = whole bars (240, 480 or 960 f); seam move at 20-40 px/f with true motion blur; entry E.out 30-50 f, exit E.in 12-24 f; seam on the downbeat.
- **Use when:** Autoplay loops for social, landing pages and product pages.
- **Avoid when:** Pieces that end on a lockup (it appears once, at the end), and loops whose first frame must work as a readable poster.

### Machine on the grid, hands off it

`ps-machine-grid-human-gaps` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, launch

Work the product does (rows inserting, items stacking, text streaming) ticks on a strict metronome, while what a person does (moving the cursor, flipping toggles, clicking) arrives on uneven, deliberating gaps, so the viewer can feel who is acting.

- **Build:** Tag every scheduled event in src/timeline.ts with who performs it: SYS for work the product does (rows inserting, items stacking, text streaming, status steps) and USER for what a person does (cursor travel, clicks, toggles, drags). SYS start frames come from b() on a fixed step: 15 f (an 8th at 120 BPM) for inserts, or 16ths via b(bar, beat, sub) for bursts. Every SYS instance uses the same curve and duration (for example a 12 f E.ui reveal) at a constant or ratcheting rate. Streamed text uses TypeOn with cps at 25-40 characters per second, or one fixed time box, and never jitters. USER start frames come from a hand-written list of uneven gaps, with at least 2x between the shortest and longest gap and no two neighbouring gaps within 15% of each other ([0, 4, 19, 37] f for four toggles, or gaps of 10, 26 and 14 f). Cursor travel runs through cursorArc (bow 0.15-0.25) on E.glide and lasts max(14, D / 20) f for a trip of D px, which keeps its peak under 60 px/f. A dwell of 6-18 f, chosen per instance with rand(seed), separates arrival from the press, and pressAt drives the click. Only the decisive press of each scene lands on a beat (±1 f); the rest of the user layer stays off the grid. Sound follows the same split: each SYS insert gets one soft tick so the metronome is heard (dropped once inserts pass about 3 per second over a bed), and USER actions stay silent except the decisive click.
- **Timing:** SYS: one event every 15 f (an 8th at 120 BPM), or every 7-8 f (16ths) in bursts; identical 12 f E.ui reveals; streams at 25-40 characters per second. USER: gaps such as 4, 15 and 18 f, or 10, 26 and 14 f; cursor travel max(14, D/20) f on E.glide, peak under 60 px/f, with motion blur above 12 px/f; dwell 6-18 f; press 12 f via pressAt; the decisive press on the beat ±1 f.
- **Use when:** Product demos where a person gives an instruction and the product or an agent responds, walkthroughs that mix input with generated output, and any sequence where automation should feel tireless next to a human.
- **Avoid when:** Pure type films or brand stings with no user in the story; polyrhythm grids, which run their own clocks; musical montages where every event must land on the beat.

### One screen direction per act

`ps-direction-per-act` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

Each act owns one direction of travel, so every entrance, exit, drift and camera ramp in it runs the same way, and the direction turns only at an act seam, where the turn itself marks the new chapter.

- **Build:** Add a DIR map beside ACT in src/timeline.ts with one unit vector per act ({x: 1, y: 0} for left to right, {x: -1, y: 0} for right to left, or {x: 0, y: -1} for an upward feed), plus a helper along(act, d) that returns {x: d * DIR.x, y: d * DIR.y}. Route every directional number through that helper. Entrances start upstream at along(act, -O), with O = 8-15% of frame width, and brake on E.out. Holds drift downstream at 0.3-1 px/f. Exits and accelerate-into-cut ramps leave downstream on E.in, and whoosh pan takes the sign of DIR.x. Inside an act nothing travels against the vector except a settle tail or a final move to centre. Across each cut inside the act, the hero leaves by the downstream edge and comes back in from the upstream edge, still travelling the same way. Turn the vector only at an act seam, on its downbeat (a seam may also keep it). Make each turn coincide with a second channel change (a polarity flip, a score section change, or the switch from imagery to type) so it reads as a new chapter rather than a continuity slip. The last act's vector delivers the lockup: the mark arrives along it and settles centred. Check it in a node test beside grid-check: sample each act's text positions at f and f + 1 from the same functions the acts use, and assert that every text element moving faster than 2 px/f has a velocity whose dot product with DIR is positive, except settle tails of at most 6 f.
- **Timing:** 2-4 vectors per film, one per act, each turn on b(n) at an act seam. Entrance offsets 8-15% of frame width (150-290 px at 1080p), braking on E.out over 30-50 f; hold drift 0.3-1 px/f downstream; exit ramps 18-24 f on E.in, reaching 17-38 px/f; counter-motion above 2 px/f lasts at most 6 f and only in settle tails.
- **Use when:** Films built from hard cuts with velocity handoffs, two-act spots (imagery, then type), runs of statements (an upward feed), and vertical films with a rising vector.
- **Avoid when:** Oners and single camera journeys, where the layout of the surface sets the direction; films whose motion is mostly radial zooms; multi-cell grids; a film with no act change, which should keep one vector throughout.

### Phrase chunks on the beat

`ps-beat-quantized-chunks` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

A line arrives in two or three chunks split by meaning, each landing exactly on the next beat, so the reading rhythm is performed by the track.

- **Build:** Split the copy into 2-3 chunks by meaning (subject | object | qualifier). Chunk k starts at b(bar, beat + k) minus half its first word's rise, so the rise's 50% frame lands on the beat. Words inside a chunk follow 4 f apart, each on a baseline line-mask rise (an overflow-hidden line box, translateY 100% to 0 on E.out with arrive()). For a calmer build, use one beat per word with a blur-to-focus reveal: opacity 0 to 1 over 8 f, blurIn from 8 px across 18 f, a 13 px rise over 28 f on E.out, plus a 1 px/f line drift. Hold the finished line for at least 36 f + 6 f per word.
- **Timing:** One beat per chunk (30 f at 120 BPM); 4 f word stagger inside a chunk; masked rise 6-8 f E.out, stretched to 10-12 f for words over 60 px tall so legible glyphs stay under 20 px/f; calm variant 20-22 f per word.
- **Use when:** Statement lines over music with a clear pulse, launch openers, and 3-7 word claims.
- **Avoid when:** No music or a free-time score, and sentences of more than 8 words.

### Spectacle, diagram, walkthrough, sign-off

`ps-four-sequence-launch` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy medium · launch

A launch film in four sequences: a short spectacle open, one concept diagram, a long real-product walkthrough and a brief brand close.

- **Build:** Split the runtime about 19/14/58/9%, each part a contiguous bar-aligned ACT in src/timeline.ts. The open (surge) gets the biggest moves and the strongest use of the accent colour. The diagram (dip) is one centred concept figure that names the idea, paced slower. The walkthrough (plateau) is 10-14 shots built from wide/close pairs: render the UI once and frame each close-up as the same composition at 4-4.5x scale on the control, with the cuts velocity-matched. The close (a small peak, then calm) replays the open's mechanic and lands the lockup. Edit the track to the same contour (`track.py edit`): its intro under the open, its break under the diagram, its body under the walkthrough, and its ending (a button or a ring) on the close.
- **Timing:** Shares 19/14/58/9% (at 30 s: about 342/252/1044/162 f). Walkthrough shot median 75-100 f; wides 90-180 f, close-ups 76-154 f at 4-4.5x. Lockup hold 90-120 f inside the close.
- **Use when:** 30-60 s launch films that have to earn attention, explain an idea and then prove it in the product.
- **Avoid when:** Spots under 15 s (use the image-then-type plan instead) and products with nothing to diagram.

### A designed hold that clicks into place

`dv-designed-hold` · pacing and structure · accent · energy calm · any

A held frame on purpose: the settled mark is bit-identical for 4 frames as it clicks into place; a stamped line sits perfectly still while only the background light pools move; a title holds over a second with under 3 px drift.

- **Build:** Recipe: no creep on the element for the hold (declare the still range); keep LightField or grain alive. Anatomy: 4-28 f of stillness; a living background layer. Sound: Silence or the voice.
- **Timing:** 4-70 f.
- **Use when:** After a landing that should feel locked.
- **Avoid when:** Long dead holds without any living layer.

### Accelerando into the climax

`ps-accelerando-to-climax` · pacing and structure · accent · energy high · launch, sting, feature

Shot lengths shrink step by step toward the climax, then one designed freeze on the track's stop resets the clock just before the payoff lands.

- **Build:** Plan the last 5-7 shots before the climax on the beat grid, each about 0.7x the length of the one before: for example 4, 3, 2, 1.5, 1 and 1 beats at 120 BPM (120, 90, 60, 45, 30 and 30 f). Text only goes on shots long enough for the copy rule, and shots without text can go down to 24 f. Each shot ends on the accelerate-into-cut ramp, scaled to its last 40% on E.in, over a rising stretch of the track (a build, or the bars before its entry). The run ends on a 12-15 f freeze sitting exactly on the track's own stop or a stop-down (`plan.py`), and the climax move starts at full speed on the next downbeat.
- **Timing:** Shots 120, 90, 60, 45, 30, 30 f (about x0.7 each, minimum 24 f without text); exit ramps on the last 40% of each shot, E.in; freeze 12-15 f on the stop; climax on the next downbeat.
- **Use when:** The run-up to a reveal, a collage burst or the lockup in launch films and stings.
- **Avoid when:** Walkthroughs where each shot carries UI that must be read, and films already cutting under 60 f per shot throughout.

### Breath envelope per card

`ps-breath-envelope` · pacing and structure · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical

Every card arrives fast and decelerates, rests through its hold while its content changes, then accelerates away and is cut on its fastest frame.

- **Build:** Drive each card's container with one summed transform of three terms. Arrival: tw(f, 0, 36, 90, 0, E.out) px of translate (or scale lmix(1.08, 1, prog(f, 0, 36))), with arrive() on vertical text moves and blurIn only while the card travels faster than 12 px/f. Hold: a linear drift of 0.4-1 px/f, or breath() from src/lib/camera.ts at about +0.06%/f, optionally with letter-spacing tightening 2-3% over 40 f on E.outSoft from the landing frame. Exit: tw(f, T-16, T, 0, 100, E.in) px (or +6% scale) with blurOut, and the hard cut on frame T, which is the exit's fastest frame. Because the terms add, speed follows a U (fast, slow, fast) and never touches zero mid-card; the hold length follows the copy rule (36 f + 6 f per word).
- **Timing:** Arrival 20-50 f E.out (default 36, peak about 15 px/f). Hold = 36 f + 6 f per word, still (a sub-pixel creep at most, 0.2 px/f@60). Exit 14-20 f E.in, reaching 19-39 px/f on the cut.
- **Use when:** Statement cards, kinetic type and feature cards in a fast-cut film; the hold rests, the arrival and the exit carry the motion.
- **Avoid when:** Dense UI that needs a dead-still read (lock the camera instead), and the final lockup hold.

### Empty ground after a cut

`ps-empty-ground-after-cut` · pacing and structure · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical

Right after some hard cuts the new stage shows for two empty frames before its type appears, a tiny palate cleanser that makes the cut read crisply without any flash.

- **Build:** On selected statement-to-statement hard cuts, not every cut, delay the incoming card's first element by 2 f: the new background is on screen at the cut frame, and the card's Sequence starts at cut + 2, its first element arriving on its normal E.out entrance. Use it where the outgoing card has already left by its own exit (an E.in move, or a fade over its last 8 f) and both stages are flat, so the two empty frames read as a breath and not as a dropped frame. Never use it on the film's first frame, where the hook has to open composed and moving.
- **Timing:** 2 empty frames at 60 fps; the incoming card starts at cut + 2 on its usual entrance; on at most a third of the cuts.
- **Use when:** Type-led films on white or flat stages with many statement cuts.
- **Avoid when:** Velocity-matched cuts, where the gap kills the momentum, and frame 0.

### The one long hold

`ps-one-long-hold` · pacing and structure · accent · energy any · launch, feature, vertical

In a film that otherwise never stops, a single key claim sits nearly still for over a second, which tells the viewer it is the line to remember.

- **Build:** Reserve exactly one statement per film for this. After it settles (words on SPR.word or src/fx/Words.tsx), hold it 60-90 f with the type effectively still: breath(t, 0.015-0.02) from src/lib/camera.ts on its container (under 0.3 px/f at the edges) and a background breathing ±3% opacity, with no new element entering. Every other shot keeps a breath envelope or a camera move, so this hold is at least twice as long as any other near-still stretch. Leave on an E.in scale creep of +6% over the last 18 f, cutting on the creep's fastest frame.
- **Timing:** Settle 20-36 f; hold 60-90 f at under 0.3 px/f; exit creep +6% over 18 f E.in. Every other near-still run stays at or under 30 f.
- **Use when:** The single claim or number the film exists to say, in a launch film or short spot that is relentless everywhere else.
- **Avoid when:** Films already built on long holds, where it stops reading as special, or when two lines compete for the slot.

### Travelling thread object

`ps-continuity-thread` · pacing and structure · signature · energy high · launch, feature

One small accent object (a dot, a packet or a streak) recurs across shots and acts, carrying the idea from problem to feature to feature as a single causal chain.

- **Build:** Build one Thread component: a round head 2-3% of frame height plus a tapered tail whose length scales with speed (tail = clamp(v * 1.5, 0, 240) px). Each scene drives it along a path (SVG getPointAtLength) with a speed curve that is always fast: E.contact into an impact or E.out into the distance. Across a cut it re-enters from the same screen side and at the same angle it left by, and it hands off by becoming the next scene's element (a check, a pin, a button fill), with squash() on contact. The full look surrounds the head with a bloom halo and shifts its tint on each beat (one beat goes violet). Use 3-5 appearances over 9-15 s at the same size every time.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Same Thread component in the single brand accent: an opaque head with a solid tapered tail and no halo or bloom, and the same hue on every beat. Impacts read through squash() and a hitPulse scale bump on the struck element rather than a flash of light. The full look relies on glow, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** 3-5 appearances of 20-60 f each; head 2-3% of frame height; travel 20-60 px/f with true motion blur; contact squash over about 8 f; hitPulse(t, 2, 5) on the struck element.
- **Use when:** Abstract or concept-led launch films whose beats are visually disconnected, and stories about value or data travelling.
- **Avoid when:** Plain UI walkthroughs where a cursor already guides the eye, since two guides compete.

### Eyes open and blink

`dv-character-life` · micro-interactions · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A character or object gets life from its eyes: an eye springs open behind an object, gets a catch-light and blinks 1-4-1 frames; a character closes its eyes for about 4 frames.

- **Build:** Recipe: lid as a clip-path driven by a spring; blink as three stepped states. Anatomy: Lid spring zeta 0.70 with 4.5 % overshoot; blink 2/10/2 f. Sound: A UI pop on the open.
- **Timing:** Open 22 f; blink 15 f.
- **Use when:** Mascots and characters.
- **Avoid when:** Blinks on a regular metronome.
